Six story functions across five voiced scenes: visual paradox, contradiction, clue, mechanism, distinct second reveal, payoff. Target 25–29 seconds including the configured sign-off; hard max 30. Keep voice, karaoke, local BGM and channel outro. No generic spoken CTA. Visual direction: Use the photoreal live-action style in visualStyle, like varied Pexels-style footage. Open on the real object and its surprising visible detail. Build five distinct camera setups: vary at least two of shot scale, angle, location, lighting and physical action between neighboring scenes. Prefer observable actions, practical macro details, human hands, and real-world context over abstract visual metaphors. For a hidden mechanism, use a plausible exposed component or demonstration prop without pretending an invented event was filmed. Keep brand signs out if accurate rendering is doubtful. Generate a distinct Gemini still and Google Flow six-second clip per voiced scene; review action, 9:16 crop and continuity before binding local MP4s. Generated shots explain sourced facts and are not documentary proof. Packaging: make the YouTube title and description curiosity-driven, a little provocative, and specific to the subject; deliver exactly the claim the video explains. The title may tease the mechanism, but do not exaggerate risk, savings, universality or a company motive beyond the facts. The description should invite one topic-specific viewer response.

Core fact: Cutting an apple exposes its flesh to oxygen and activates enzymatic browning.
Second reveal: Acidic lemon juice can slow the visible browning reaction.
Opening shot: one fresh apple slice beside a browning slice. Show it as a believable real-world shot, immediately legible in the first frame. Do not reveal the internal mechanism in the opening. Use different real camera compositions and meaningful subject motion for the clue, mechanism, second reveal and payoff. Do not use an imaginary accident, simulated rescue, or fake news-style scene. 
Fact boundaries: Browning is not proof that an apple is unsafe; timing varies by variety and conditions.
